title: Future Champions Sports Complex damaged by possible tornado - NewsBreak
text: Jacksonville’s “happy place” took a direct hit on Wednesday. Future Champions Sports Complex, just a few hundred yards from Memorial Hospital , was in the path of a possible tornado that hit Jacksonville at noon. Co-owner Kristin Jamison said no one was injured at the facility. Four of the six fields sustained damage. Fences were twisted and blown over. The roofs of dugouts were blown away. A set of bleachers from one field was deposited upside-down in the outfield of another. Black netting meant to stop foul balls was left tattered and blowing in the wind. Pieces of insulation and other debris clung to fences throughout the facility. Corn planted north of the parking lot was flattened. Jacksonville Police and Fire personnel responded to the scene to evaluate the situation. Jamison was surveying the damage less than an hour after the tornado struck. Read also: What it takes for the National Weather Service to confirm a tornado “That is the true bright spot in the situation, is that we had two employees who were helping get ready for this weekend and they were Johnny on the spot to get to a safe location and emerged unscathed,” she said. “And we can just thank God that they are in perfect shape right now.” Jamison was not at the facility when the storm blew through. She had just finished watching her daughter perform at a J’ettes pom clinic and was heading to her house to drop off her daughter when the tornado siren went off. “We, of course, took shelter, and that's when I got a call from my husband that he was literally watching the tornado rip through the 28 acres of our property,” Jamison said. “He was in his truck. We were trying to get ready — we have 50 teams coming this weekend, so he was getting food ready for the weekend, and he was heading toward Beardstown at the time and saw what was happening and stopped.” Jamison said someone sent her a picture of the damage before she got to the facility. “It really didn't do the magnitude of destruction justice, if that makes sense,” she said. “As I walked up … I was in tears driving here, and in even more tears when I came upon every inch of this place that we worked so hard to try to improve since we took ownership in 2020.” It was the second major tragedy to befall the complex. The Jamisons purchased the property just before the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, canceling the first several months of tournaments at the facility. The damage to the fields was stunning, given that it’s an outdoor facility. Future Swings, an indoor hitting facility on the north side of Walnut Street, was sliced in two, showing the direct path of the tornado. Future Champions was in its fifth season since being bought by the couple. Games had been played at the 28-acre complex within just the past week, and they had advertised "Wing Night" just hours before the storm. “Parts of our restaurant are damaged, of course, and then as you look at about three of our fields, they're definitely in need of repair,” Jamison said. The tornado touched down just a few hundred yards away from The Pointe at Jacksonville, an assisted living facility just south of the sports fields. “You can see the path of the tornado,” Jamison said. “And the other thing I think about, just looking at it, is how close that was to The Pointe and the folks that are living there, and then how close this is to the hospital. And while this is tough for us, it is a miracle that it didn't hurt people.” As they assessed the damage, Jamison and her husband were scrambling to make arrangements for a tournament scheduled for Future Champions this weekend. “We're still trying to process what needs to happen next,” Jamison said. “My phone has been buzzing since I walked up with people asking if they could help. How do we roll up our sleeves and get things cleaned up? And of course, we have to wait for the insurance representatives to do their work, but it's great to know that we live in a community where people are ready to help at a moment’s notice.” Jamison has spoken to representatives at Jacksonville High School, Routt, Illinois College and the YMCA trying to find fields for this weekend. “Of course, people have made plans,” she said. “They have hotel rooms. They want to be here in Jacksonville this weekend, so if there is any way we can make it happen, we will do that. “This was truly just — I don't even have the words for it because I'm still processing what I see when I look around,” Jamison said. “Dugouts completely flattened, some of the turf just taken up from the wind, a bleacher from one field on another field. It's devastating.” Sign up for Jacksonville Journal-Courier newsletters here Read the original article on myjournalcourier.com
